FIELD NOTES

Where the depth comes from

Find a corner

A corner changes brightness in two directions. The tracker looks for these distinctive patches and searches for their counterparts in the second image.

Measure the shift

With a level camera sliding sideways, matching corners stay on nearly the same row. The solver checks this constraint and discards ambiguous matches.

Intersect the views

Depth equals focal length times camera travel divided by horizontal pixel shift. Tiny shifts give uncertain distances. A camera turning in place supplies no baseline.

Model assumptions and uploaded video

This experiment uses a calibrated sideways slide, a fixed focal length and a stationary scene. For uploads, the solver estimates relative camera pose from matching patches using an assumed focal length. It recovers shape up to an unknown scale. Use a short, steady clip with textured surfaces and some sideways travel. Large jumps, moving objects or zoom can produce incorrect depths. Video is processed on your device.
